verdict.rationale: Daytona docs say each sandbox runs in isolation with a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack and allocated vCPU/RAM/disk. They also offer VM sandboxes with a dedicated Linux or Windows VM, plus a per-sandbox egress firewall, which amounts to a documented VM-level boundary. Missing for 10: no documentation of the underlying isolation technology (hypervisor/microVM type) or a threat model, unclear whether default container sandboxes get the same hard boundary as VM sandboxes, and no independent or hands-on corroboration.
